name: Swamp cabbage (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Swamp cabbage (Ipomoea aquatica) [Vegetables] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DUKE, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 169301 (Waterspinach, raw; SR Legacy NDB 11482)
Umar, Ekwenye et al. 2007, Nutritional Composition of Water Spinach (Ipomoea aquatica) Leaves, J. Applied Sci. doi:10.3923/jas.2007.803.809
Austin D.F. 2007, Water Spinach (Ipomoea aquatica, Convolvulaceae): A Food Gone Wild, Economic Botany review
Malakar & Choudhury 2015, anti-nutritional factors of fresh Karamwa (Ipomoea aquatica) leaves (oxalate 125 mg/100 g fresh)
Horizon e-Publishing PST, comparative oxalic-acid levels in fresh/processed water spinach (fresh 250 mg/100 g)
Frontiers in Nutrition 2023, Chemical/biochemical characterization of Ipomoea aquatica, doi:10.3389/fnut.2023.1304903
provenance.curation_notes: Water spinach is a low-sugar leafy green: with net non-fiber carbohydrate ~1 g/100 g, the dominant assimilable carbon/energy for a microbe is NOT free sugars but the free/protein amino acids (Asp, Glu, Ala, Leu, Lys, Thr, Val most abundant) and organic acids — chiefly oxalic acid (125-250 mg/100 g), with malic and citric acid also present (both absent from the original FooDB profile). Mineral/vitamin panel is USDA fresh-weight (FDC 169301); high in vitamin C (55 mg), provitamin-A carotenoids, K,
curation_added: oxalic acid (dominant organic acid, quantified 125-250 mg/100 g)
individual free sugars: D-glucose, D-fructose, sucrose
full quantitative USDA amino-acid profile (Trp, Thr, Ile, Leu, Lys, Met, Cys, Phe, Tyr, Val, His, Ala, Asp, Gly, Pro, Ser)
quantitative minerals (K, Na, Ca, Mg, P, Fe, Zn, Cu, Mn, Se)
quantitative vitamins (C, B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, folate, vitamin A)
total protein, total carbohydrate, dietary fiber, total fat, water

curation_removed.reason: Compartmentalized model/BiGG artifact (subcellular localization), not a food-composition descriptor; duplicate of iron.

curation_removed.name: Co2+
curation_removed.reason: Cobalt ion — non-nutritive trace element for this food; FooDB/model noise, water spinach is not a cobalt source.

curation_removed.name: Nickel
curation_removed.reason: Non-nutritive trace/contaminant element, not a growth nutrient of this vegetable.

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
